ARTICLE HIGHLIGHTS • Why did we undertake this study? Patients with schizophrenia treated with second-generation antipsychotics are at high risk of prediabetes and metabolic dysfunction, yet effective interventions remain limited. • What is the specific question we wanted to answer? Does semaglutide improve insulin sensitivity/resistance, insulin secretion, and other glucose-metabolic outcomes in this high-risk population? • What did we find? In a randomized controlled trial of 154 participants, semaglutide significantly improved insulin sensitivity, reduced insulin resistance, and lowered fasting glucose compared with placebo. These benefits were largely mediated by substantial weight loss (∼9.2 kg). β-Cell function showed only modest, nonsignificant improvement. • What are the implications of our findings? Semaglutide may represent an effective strategy to mitigate antipsychotic-induced metabolic dysfunction in patients with schizophrenia and prediabetes.

reported_results.text: Semaglutide Effects on Insulin Sensitivity and β-Cell Function in Patients With Schizophrenia, Prediabetes, and Obesity Treated With Second-Generation Antipsychotics: Findings From the HISTORI Trial, a 30-Week Randomized, Placebo-Controlled Trial With Semaglutide 1.0 mg Weekly Ashok A.

Compared with placebo, semaglutide significantly reduced fasting glucose (−0.87 mmol/L [95% CI −1.15, −0.59]; P < 0.001), improved insulin sensitivity (8.60 [5.82, 13.65]; P = 0.001), and lowered insulin resistance (−0.69 [−1.00, −0.20]; P = 0.006).

In contrast, insulin sensitivity increasedsignificantly in the semaglutidetreated group (10.08 [5.82, 14.33]) compared with the placebo-treated group (1.48 [−2.79, 5.75]), resulting in a significant treatment effect averaging 8.60 (5.82,13.65;P=0.001)(Fig.1).

[95% CI, −1.66, 17.65]) and remained unchanged in the placebo group (−0.10 [−8.54, 8.33]), but overall, semaglutide caused a nonsignificant increase in β-cell function (8.10 [−1.66, 20.22]; P = 0.19) (Table 2).

At week 30, semaglutide significantly increased insulin sensitivity (mean difference 8.60 [95% CI 5.82, 13.65]; P = 0.001). β-Cell function showed a modest, nonsignificant improvement (mean difference 8.60 [–2.53, 19.73]; P = 0.13).
